title: Apologizing plainly
tomorrow: tara posts something mean about simran. can she forgive that?

segments.voice: Yesterday, listening in conversation: hear someone all the way to the end. Kiran finished her story. Now Simran has one small thing of her own to own.
screen: `LISTEN FULLY.` → `NOW SIMRAN HAS SOMETHING TO OWN.`

segments.voice: Sorry, but. Two words that undo the first one. Simran knows exactly which buts she wants. Sorry, but everyone was posting. Sorry, but I never sent the joke. Sorry, but it was only an emoji. All true. All of them sliding the weight off her and back onto the chat. Her face goes hot just drafting it. Bebe Jaswant, at the stove, doesn't turn around. Ask the way we ask at the end of Ardas, she says. No buts in it.
screen: `SORRY, BUT.` → `EVERY BUT SLIDES THE WEIGHT AWAY.` → `BEBE: NO BUTS IN IT.`

segments.voice: Here's what Bebe means. Ardas is the prayer Sikhs say standing, hands pressed together, and tradition makes room in it to ask pardon after a reading for any mistakes: a letter added, a letter missed, a word said wrong. Bhul chuk, slips and errors. It's said simply. Nobody explains why they slipped. In the Granth, in Raag Suhi, Guru Nanak puts it even plainer: I am not good, and no one is bad. That's the posture of an apology without excuses. Not I'm the worst person alive. Just: I'm not the good one in this story, and you're not the bad one. Feel what each version does in the body. The excuse lifts your shoulders, ready to defend. The plain sorry lets them drop. The heat in your face is real, and it passes. And here's the surprising part to tell a friend: the plain apology is shorter. Sorry, but takes a paragraph. Sorry takes one breath. So Simran calls. I put a laughing face on that thread before I thought. I'm sorry. That's all. Kiran is quiet a second. Then: thanks for saying it like that.
screen: `ARDAS: PARDON FOR SLIPS.` · `GURU NANAK: I AM NOT GOOD.` · `SHOULDERS UP, SHOULDERS DOWN.` · `SORRY TAKES ONE BREATH.` · then, large: `SORRY, PLAINLY.`

segments.voice: Sit or stand tall and press your palms together at your chest, the way people stand for Ardas. Bring to mind one person you owe a plain sorry, and say it out loud, quietly, one sentence with no but. Then let your hands rest and your shoulders drop for the sit.
Apologizing plainly. Sorry, with no but after it. Bhul chuk: slips and errors, owned.
Sorry, plainly: one breath, no but, and then let the quiet do the rest. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Sikhs say Ardas standing with palms joined, and it is customary after a reading to ask pardon for any slips (bhul chuk) in it, simply and without explanation.

fork.setup: you snapped at your little brother, and you were also really tired. he's sulking in his room. what does a plain apology sound like?
options: "i'm sorry i snapped at you." then stop.
"i'm sorry, but i was exhausted and you were loud."
"i'm the worst sibling ever. i'm so, so sorry."
fork.reveal: the tiredness is true, and it's still a but. a plain sorry owns your part in one breath, without excuses or a show of self-blame.

chat.says: kiran's cool with me now. but tara's mad i 'took kiran's side.' do i apologize to her too??
options: only for anything you actually did wrong, plainly. not for the rest.

chat.meaning: A plain apology owns your own part, without excuses, and doesn't take on what isn't yours.
